name: Halo Dynamics Softshell BCI Pullover
description:
Halo Dynamics makes hardware and, increasingly, the clothing designed to interface with it. The Softshell BCI Pullover is a crew-neck pullover in a matte charcoal softshell fabric that looks, at a glance, like a normal athletic top. Look closer and you'll see the subtle port-access panels at the base of the skull — two small magnetic flap covers, flush with the fabric, that allow BCI maintenance and hardware access without removing the garment. The fabric itself has a low-conductivity inner lining that reduces interference with surface-mounted BCI hardware. It's not glamorous tech, but it's practical.

The cut is clean and slightly athletic. It works as a standalone top or an underlayer. Halo Dynamics includes it in the standard 'adaptation kit' sold alongside their mid-range BCI implants, which means a significant percentage of Tier 3 BCI users own one. It reads as tech-adjacent without screaming it — someone wearing this is probably augmented, but not necessarily heavily.
functionality: BCI port-access panels at skull base with magnetic closures. Low-conductivity inner lining reduces electromagnetic interference with surface-mounted neural hardware.
what_it_says: You're augmented. You've thought about what you wear around your hardware. You're practical about it.
worn_by: people who want aug-compatible clothing without looking like they're trying
story_hooks: A batch of Halo Dynamics Softshell Pullovers was recalled quietly after reports that the low-conductivity lining was interfering with third-party BCI hardware in unexpected ways — not just dampening interference but blocking certain signal types entirely. Some users found this feature, not a flaw.
Someone has been modifying the BCI access panels on secondhand Softshells to include a passive signal skimmer. The modifications are invisible to the naked eye.

A Tier 5 intelligence analyst was found dead wearing this pullover, which is unusual — people at his level wear bespoke. The Halo Dynamics serial number traces back to a purchase made under a false name three days before his death.

physical_description.visual_profile: A streamlined crew-neck pullover with athletic undertones and subtle technological integration. The silhouette is clean and understated, appearing at first glance like premium sportswear until the careful observer notices the barely-visible port-access geometry at the nape. Projects quiet competence and practical augmentation without flashiness.
physical_description.fit: Slightly athletic and tailored—fitted through the shoulders and chest without compression, with a relaxed taper at the torso. Designed to layer or stand alone. Mobility-focused seams suggest functional design rather than fashion-forward cut.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte charcoal softshell synthetic blend—durable, moisture-wicking, with embedded low-conductivity inner lining for BCI hardware compatibility
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost muted surface with a subtle technical weave visible on close inspection. The matte finish absorbs light rather than reflecting it. Inner lining has a slightly tacky, anti-static texture.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat charcoal gray with zero contrast elements. Deliberately neutral and corporate. Magnetic flap covers at base of skull match the fabric tone exactly.
physical_description.closures: Pullover construction with seamless crew neckline. Two subtle magnetic flap ports at base of skull—barely raised, friction-fit flush with the fabric.
distinctive_features: Twin magnetic port-access panels at the base of the skull for BCI maintenance
Low-conductivity inner lining visible along collar and cuffs
Minimal branding—small Halo Dynamics logo embossed on left chest
Subtle grid texture on inner lining suggests circuit geometry
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—mid-range BCI ecosystem hardware. Accessible augmentation tech for working-class professionals and technical workers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by BCI users, systems integrators, technical workers, medical augmentation clients. Signals someone augmented but not heavily modded. Reads as 'adapted' rather than 'enhanced.' Common in corporate offices, medical facilities, and tech labs across the GLMZ.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to well-maintained. Halo includes these in adaptation kits, so most are relatively new. May show minor wear around port covers from repeated access cycles. No intentional distressing—this is maintenance gear, treated with care.

image_prompt: Charcoal matte softshell pullover on a sleek androgynous model with visible subdermal circuitry beneath translucent temple skin, shot against a dark industrial GLMZ backdrop of stacked server cores and soft blue diagnostic lighting. Close detail on the back of the neck showing the two magnetic BCI port flaps. Moody cyberpunk fashion photography with cool color grading, shallow depth of field focusing on the port details. Model's posture is neutral and professional. --ar 2:3 --v 6
